subject.title: [Bug]:  Session status blind spot | Sessions in done state excluded from context saturation monitoring — agents run dead for hours undetected

question: Should native monitoring alert on saturated terminal `done` sessions, and should the response be warning-only, operator notification, cleanup, or recovery?
rationale: Source inspection shows the data exists but no native alert path consumes it; threshold, alert target, and recovery behavior are product/operations choices rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Add Warning-Only Diagnostics
options.body: Surface saturated terminal session rows through health or diagnostic attention without automatic cleanup or recovery.

options.title: Add Recovery Or Cleanup
options.body: Treat saturated terminal sessions as actionable zombie sessions and trigger a maintainer-approved cleanup or recovery path.

options.title: Keep Manual Operator Workflow
options.body: Leave native monitoring unchanged and document `openclaw sessions compact` or cleanup as the supported operational response.

recommendation.title: Add Warning-Only Diagnostics
recommendation.body: Surface saturated terminal session rows through health or diagnostic attention without automatic cleanup or recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: The session liveness diagnostic surface introduced in the merged diagnostics PR is the closest current product decision boundary for this alert contract.
